speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand the cause, can you tell me if your stool has become pale, clay-colored, or acholic recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase, GGT, and Liver Enzymes. Can you also tell me if you have noticed any jaundice or if the baby has been passing any dark urine?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Requested liver function tests: Bilirubin, Alkaline Phosphatase, GGT, and Liver Enzymes are not included in the provided data. Clinical note: No observation of jaundice or dark urine was recorded in the available examination data; primary findings indicate abdominal distension, tympanitis, and a transition zone suggestive of Hirschsprung disease).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease. The clinical presentation of abdominal distension, tympany, feeding difficulties, and the absence of liver pathology strongly supports a congenital aganglionic megacolon. I recommend an abdominal X-Ray to confirm the transition zone.
